A default command runs automatically on a subsystem whenever no other command needs it.

Think of your drivetrain: you spend most of the match driving manually. The drive subsystem should always respond to joysticks unless a path-following command takes over.

Instead of schedule()-ing a RunCommand that runs forever, you set it as the default command: subsystem.setDefaultCommand(command).

The scheduler interrupts the default command when any other command requires the subsystem. When that command finishes, the default resumes automatically. No manual scheduling, no restarting after interruptions.

Open DefaultCommandOpMode.java. It extends CommandOpMode with an empty initialize().

Open DriveSubsystem.java. It's already filled in with the mecanum drive from the gamepad input lesson — four motors and a drive(forward, strafe, turn) method.

You only need to write the OpMode.

Open DriveSubsystem.java.

It declares four private DcMotor fields and gets them from the HardwareMap in the constructor, reversing the left-side motors.

drive(forward, strafe, turn) applies the exact mecanum formula from the gamepad input lesson. stop() sets all four motors to 0. periodic() is empty.

You don't need to change anything here.

In DefaultCommandOpMode's initialize(), create a DriveSubsystem and a GamepadEx from gamepad1.

Call drive.setDefaultCommand() with a RunCommand. The RunCommand reads the gamepad sticks (forward = -leftY, strafe = leftX, turn = rightX) and calls drive.drive(forward, strafe, turn) each tick.

A default command must require its subsystem, so pass drive to the RunCommand constructor: new RunCommand(() -> { ... }, drive).

No schedule() call needed — the default command runs automatically.

Also add telemetry display and telemetry.update() inside the RunCommand so you can see it's running.

Bind the A button using GamepadEx. When pressed, schedule a command that requires the drive subsystem.

Use a SequentialCommandGroup: an InstantCommand that calls drive.drive(-0.5, 0, 0) (backward), a WaitCommand of 2000ms, and an InstantCommand that calls drive.stop().

Pass drive to each InstantCommand's constructor so they require the subsystem.

Requiring the drive subsystem means the scheduler must interrupt the default command — you can't have two commands using the same subsystem.

When the sequence finishes, the default drive command resumes automatically.

Start the OpMode. Drive with the gamepad sticks — the default command is running.

Press A — the robot drives backward for 2 seconds. The default command pauses automatically.

After 2 seconds, control returns to the gamepad. The default command resumes without you doing anything.

This is why real teams use default commands for their drivetrain: drive normally with joysticks, and autonomous sequences take over temporarily without breaking manual control.
